title: Preparation, Storage and Use of Positive and Negative Controls for DDNS
author: Joyce Akello

steps.title: Reconstitute CVA20 Positive Control
steps.instruction: Reconstitute the lyophilized CVA20 material within a Class II Microbiological Safety Cabinet (MSCII).

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL of nuclease free water (NFW) to the vial containing the lyophilized CVA20.
Vortex briefly until the material completely dissolves into a colorless liquid.

steps.title: Aliquot and Store Positive Control
steps.instruction: Divide the reconstituted solution into single-use aliquots for long-term storage.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot the solution into 30 µl volumes in 1.5 mL sterile, DNase/RNase free eppendorf tubes.
Label tubes with the reconstitution date.
Store aliquots at -20°C (stable for up to 5 weeks).

steps.title: Prepare Positive Extraction Control
steps.instruction: Prepare the CVA20 positive extraction control for the RNA extraction batch.

substeps.instruction: Retrieve a 30 µl aliquot of CVA20 from the -20°C freezer.
Thaw the aliquot at room temperature inside the MSCII cabinet.
Add 270 µl of NFW and pipette up and down to mix.
Aliquot 300 µl of nuclease free water (NFW) into a sterile 1.5 mL DNase/RNase free Eppendorf tube labelled ExNTC.

steps.title: Perform RNA Extraction and Storage
steps.instruction: Extract RNA from samples and controls and store the resulting elutes.

substeps.instruction: Perform RNA extraction of the samples in parallel with the positive and negative controls.
Keep purified RNA elutes on ice during processing.
Store elutes at -80°C if not for immediate use in the DDNS protocol.
